Did the chef choose the 'oy'sters at the fresh seafood market this morning? 

 No, he didn’t. He chose the 'oy'sters yesterday and froze them.

Did the supervisor check the fermentation p'o'int before preparing the dosa batter? 

 Yes, he did. He checked the fermentation p'o'int before starting the process.

Did the manufacturer v'oi'd the warranty of the sealing machine last week?

examples.sentence:
___________ were you when the accident happened? 

  In the dough processing section , close to the fermentation room.

content.sentence:
___________ exactly did the accident happen? 

 It was around noon, just before the lunch break bell.

___________ got injured? 

 A trainee from the new batch.

___________ did it happen? 

 It happened in the welding workshop, next to the emergency exit.

___________ did he get injured? 

 The trainee put his hand too close to the grinder.

___________ hand got injured, the left or the right? 

 The fingers of his right hand were cut.

___________ did the instructor do when it happened? 

 The instructor switched off the machine and moved the students away.

___________ trainees were present in the welding workshop at the time of the accident? 

 All 35 trainees were present.

___________ wasn’t he wearing safety gloves? 

 The instructor forgot to give them at the start of the class.

___________ did the doctor take to arrive at the welding workshop? 

 The doctor arrived within five minutes of the call.

___________ should you stand from machines that are operating? 

 The safety rules say we must stand at least one metre away.

Questions.question: Why did the safety inspector ask about the accident?
Questions.answer: To accurately document the incident and submit an accident report.
options: To find out who was responsible for the accident and submit a report.
To check if the workshop was overcrowded.
To accurately document the incident and submit an accident report.

Questions.question: What detail most strongly suggests that the accident could have been prevented?
Questions.answer: The absence of cut-resistant gloves during machine operation.
options: The absence of two instructors in the room to supervise.
The absence of cut-resistant gloves during machine operation.
The use of a fish-scaling machine nearby.

Questions.question: Which factor directly contributed to the trainee losing control while working?
options: The size of the pieces of meat.

Questions.question: What was the immediate response of the instructor that prevented further injury?
options: Clearing the room of the other trainees.

Questions.question: What does the trainee’s final response show about his attitude after the accident?
Questions.answer: He understands the importance of personal responsibility and safety compliance.
options: He believes accidents are unavoidable in food processing.
He understands the importance of personal responsibility and safety compliance.
He expects stricter supervision from instructors.

activity_b.text: I understand there was an accident here yesterday at around 9 a.m.
When exactly did the accident take place?
The accident happened yesterday at 10.25 a.m., during the morning practical session.
It happened in the food processing room, near the meat preparation counter.
Our instructor and two other trainees were in the room.
They were working nearby on a fish-scaling machine.
I used the meat slicer to cut mutton into cubes.
The surface of the meat slicer was slightly wet, and my hand slipped while I guided the meat forward.
The blade cut the tip of my ring finger.
I wore a protective apron, a face shield and non-slip safety shoes, but I forgot to wear cut-resistant protection gloves.
He stopped the machine immediately, cleaned the wound, applied antiseptic solution, and dressed it with cotton and a bandage.
The doctor examined the injury, gave me a tetanus injection, prescribed some medication, and advised me to rest.
We should always wear all personal protection equipment, keep work surfaces dry, and follow safety instructions carefully.
